paper_title: Mechanistic Understanding and Mitigation of Language Confusion in   English-Centric Large Language Models
caption: Distribution of Important Neurons Associated with Confusion Points in Llama3-8B. (a) Distribution of the top 300 most important FFN neurons across layers for an individual Chinese prompt “UTF8gbsn请解释拆东墙补西墙的意思。(Please explain `UTF8gbsn拆东墙补西墙.')” from Aya. (b) Aggregated distribution of important neuron scores across all Chinese test samples in Aya.
model_annotation: The figure presents two line plots, (a) and (b), both illustrating the distribution of important neurons associated with confusion points in the Llama3-8B model, with the x-axis representing the model layer (ranging from 0 to 35 in both plots, with tick marks at intervals of 5) and the y-axis representing the count of important neurons (in plot (a) ranging from 0 to 100, and in plot (b) from 0 to 175, both on linear scales). In plot (a), titled "Individual Case," a blue line with circular markers represents the count of the top 300 most important FFN value neurons for a single Chinese prompt from the Aya dataset. The count remains near zero for layers 0 through 25, then increases to approximately 20 at layer 26, dips slightly to around 10 at layer 27, rises to about 25 at layer 28, then climbs sharply to 80 at layer 30 and reaches 100 at layer 32. In plot (b), titled "Aggregated Neuron Scores," a green line with circular markers shows the aggregated count of important FFN value neurons across all Chinese test samples in Aya. The count remains near zero for layers 0 through 25, then increases to approximately 5 at layer 26, rises to about 10 at layer 27, increases further to around 20 at layer 28, then jumps to 50 at layer 29, and sharply rises to 150 at layer 30 and 175 at layer 32. Both plots show a similar trend of low neuron importance in early layers and a sharp increase in the final layers, with plot (b) exhibiting higher overall counts due to aggregation.
